title: Plant anatomy
group: BIO-EVOL / BIO-ECOL / BIO-PLANT — Evolution, Ecology & Plants
examples: What is the main difference between a monocot and a dicot leaf?
How does secondary growth change the size of a plant stem?
Can you show me a diagram comparing the cross-section of both types?

explain.say: Today we are looking at how plants are built inside.
First we compare monocots and dicots in their root structure.
Next we look at the stem cross-section differences.
Now we discuss secondary growth, which increases stem width.

items: Vascular cambium produces xylem and phloem

explain.say: A real life example is observing a tree trunk over many years.
A common mistake is thinking all plants grow the same way.

faq.q: What is the main difference between the vascular bundles in monocots and dicots?
faq.a: In monocots, the vascular bundles are scattered throughout the stem. In dicots, they are arranged in a distinct ring.
asks: Are the bundles scattered or in a ring?

faq.q: What tissue is responsible for secondary growth in stems?
faq.a: The vascular cambium is the lateral meristem responsible for secondary growth. It produces new xylem and phloem.
asks: What causes the stem to get wider?
Which layer makes the plant thicker?

faq.q: Does secondary growth happen in all plants?
faq.a: No, not all plants undergo secondary growth. For example, many grasses do not show this pattern.
asks: Can all plants get wider like trees?
Is secondary growth universal in plants?

faq.q: Are the roots of monocots and dicots different?
faq.a: Yes, while both have roots, the arrangement of vascular tissues differs between the two groups.

faq.q: What is the function of the vascular cambium?
faq.a: The vascular cambium's main job is to produce secondary xylem and secondary phloem. This increases the girth of the plant.

facts: Monocots often have parallel leaf venation.
Dicots typically have net-like leaf venation.
Secondary growth is characterized by the activity of the vascular cambium.
The vascular bundles in dicots form a distinct ring in the stem cross-section.

quiz.say: A plant with scattered vascular bundles in its stem is most likely a:
quiz.why: Monocots are defined by having scattered vascular bundles throughout their stem.

wrong.1: Dicots have vascular bundles arranged in a distinct ring.
wrong.2: Gymnosperms are a group, not defined by bundle arrangement.
wrong.3: Herbaceous describes the plant type, not the internal structure.

quiz.say: The increase in stem width over years is primarily due to:
quiz.why: The cambium is the lateral meristem responsible for producing secondary tissues that increase width.

wrong.1: The apical meristem is responsible for increasing the plant's length, not width.
wrong.2: Xylem transports water and is part of the structure, not the growth mechanism itself.
wrong.3: Phloem transports sugars and is also a transported tissue, not the growth layer.

quiz.say: If a plant shows strong evidence of secondary growth, it suggests:
quiz.why: Secondary growth leads to the formation of thick, supportive wood, indicating a woody habit.

wrong.1: Reproduction is a life cycle event, not directly measured by secondary growth.
wrong.2: Secondary growth occurs in both dicots and some monocots, so it is not exclusive to monocots.
wrong.3: Secondary growth affects the stem, but the plant must still have roots to survive.
